# Extending langgraphr

langgraphr gives you the building blocks. This guide shows how to write reusable R helper functions that add higher-level abstractions — message management, prompt templates, structured output, custom reducers, and more.

---

## Message Helpers

### Build message lists

langgraphr uses plain R lists for messages. These helpers make them easier to construct:

```r
#' Create a system message
sys_msg <- function(content) {
  list(role = "system", content = content)
}

#' Create a user message
user_msg <- function(content) {
  list(role = "user", content = content)
}

#' Create an assistant message
assistant_msg <- function(content) {
  list(role = "assistant", content = content)
}

#' Create a tool result message
tool_msg <- function(content, tool_call_id = NULL) {
  msg <- list(role = "tool", content = content)
  if (!is.null(tool_call_id)) msg$tool_call_id <- tool_call_id
  msg
}

# Usage
messages <- list(
  sys_msg("You are a helpful assistant."),
  user_msg("What is R?")
)
result <- lg_call_model(messages)
```

### Conversation builder

```r
#' Build a conversation from a simpler interface
conversation <- function() {
  msgs <- list()

  list(
    system = function(content) {
      msgs <<- c(msgs, list(sys_msg(content)))
      invisible(self)
    },
    user = function(content) {
      msgs <<- c(msgs, list(user_msg(content)))
      invisible(self)
    },
    assistant = function(content) {
      msgs <<- c(msgs, list(assistant_msg(content)))
      invisible(self)
    },
    messages = function() msgs,
    send = function() {
      lg_call_model(msgs)
    }
  )
}

# Usage
conv <- conversation()
conv$system("You are a code reviewer.")
conv$user("Review this function: add <- function(a, b) a + b")
response <- conv$send()
```

## Prompt Templates

### Template engine

```r
#' Create a prompt template
#' @param template String with {placeholders}
#' @return A function that fills in the template
prompt_template <- function(template) {
  function(...) {
    args <- list(...)
    result <- template
    for (name in names(args)) {
      result <- gsub(paste0("{", name, "}"), args[[name]], result, fixed = TRUE)
    }
    result
  }
}

# Usage
summarize_prompt <- prompt_template(
  "Summarize the following {type} in {max_points} key points:\n\n{content}"
)

prompt <- summarize_prompt(type = "article", max_points = 3, content = "...")
result <- lg_call_model(list(user_msg(prompt)))
```

### Few-shot prompt builder

```r
#' Build a few-shot prompt with examples
#' @param instruction System instruction
#' @param examples List of list(input, output) pairs
#' @return A function(query) that builds the full prompt
few_shot <- function(instruction, examples) {
  function(query) {
    msgs <- list(sys_msg(instruction))

    for (ex in examples) {
      msgs <- c(msgs, list(
        user_msg(ex$input),
        assistant_msg(ex$output)
      ))
    }

    c(msgs, list(user_msg(query)))
  }
}

# Usage
classifier <- few_shot(
  instruction = "Classify the sentiment as POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, or NEUTRAL.",
  examples = list(
    list(input = "I love this product!", output = "POSITIVE"),
    list(input = "Terrible experience.", output = "NEGATIVE"),
    list(input = "It arrived on Tuesday.", output = "NEUTRAL")
  )
)

result <- lg_call_model(classifier("The quality exceeded my expectations"))
```

## Structured Output

LangGraph uses Pydantic for structured output. In R, you can enforce structure with prompt engineering and parsing.

### JSON output

```r
#' Call the model with a JSON schema and parse the result
#' @param messages Message list
#' @param schema Named list describing the expected JSON structure
#' @return Parsed JSON as R list
lg_call_structured <- function(messages, schema) {
  # Add JSON instruction to the system message
  schema_str <- jsonlite::toJSON(schema, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)

  messages[[1]]$content <- paste(
    messages[[1]]$content,
    "\n\nRespond with ONLY valid JSON matching this structure:",
    schema_str,
    "\nDo not include markdown code blocks or any other text."
  )

  raw <- lg_call_model(messages, temperature = 0)

  # Clean and parse
  cleaned <- gsub("```json|```", "", raw)
  cleaned <- trimws(cleaned)

  tryCatch(
    jsonlite::fromJSON(cleaned),
    error = function(e) {
      # Retry once with explicit reminder
      messages[[length(messages) + 1]] <- assistant_msg(raw)
      messages[[length(messages) + 1]] <- user_msg(
        "That was not valid JSON. Return ONLY a JSON object matching the schema."
      )
      raw2 <- lg_call_model(messages, temperature = 0)
      cleaned2 <- gsub("```json|```", "", raw2)
      jsonlite::fromJSON(trimws(cleaned2))
    }
  )
}

# Usage
schema <- list(
  sentiment = "string (POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, NEUTRAL)",
  confidence = "number (0-1)",
  key_topics = "array of strings"
)

result <- lg_call_structured(
  list(sys_msg("Analyze the sentiment of the user message."),
       user_msg("The new R package is amazing — fast and well-documented!")),
  schema
)
# $sentiment: "POSITIVE"
# $confidence: 0.95
# $key_topics: ["R package", "performance", "documentation"]
```

### R-to-JSON schema

```r
#' Convert an R list schema description to a JSON schema string
#' @param fields Named list of list(type, description)
to_json_schema <- function(fields) {
  properties <- lapply(fields, function(f) {
    list(type = f$type, description = f$description %||% "")
  })
  list(
    type = "object",
    properties = properties,
    required = names(fields)
  )
}

# Usage
schema <- to_json_schema(list(
  name = list(type = "string", description = "Person's full name"),
  age = list(type = "number", description = "Age in years"),
  skills = list(type = "array", description = "List of skills")
))
```

## Custom Reducers

langgraphr supports `overwrite` and `append` reducers. Here is how to simulate more complex reducer behavior in node functions.

### Max reducer (keep the maximum value)

```r
# Instead of a custom "max" reducer, do this in the node:
max_node <- function(state) {
  current <- state$score %||% 0
  new_score <- compute_score()
  final_score <- max(current, new_score)

  list(updates = list(score = final_score))  # overwrite with max
}
```

### Merge reducer (combine two data frames)

```r
merge_node <- function(state) {
  existing <- state$data %||% data.frame()
  new_rows <- fetch_new_data()

  merged <- rbind(existing, new_rows)

  list(updates = list(data = merged))  # overwrite with merged
}
```

### Deduplicate reducer (keep unique items in a list)

```r
dedupe_node <- function(state) {
  items <- state$items %||% list()

  # Add new item
  new_item <- get_new_item()
  all_items <- c(items, list(new_item))

  # Deduplicate by content
  seen <- c()
  unique_items <- list()
  for (item in all_items) {
    key <- digest::digest(item)  # or jsonlite::toJSON(item)
    if (!(key %in% seen)) {
      seen <- c(seen, key)
      unique_items <- c(unique_items, list(item))
    }
  }

  list(updates = list(items = unique_items))  # overwrite with deduplicated
}
```

## State Utilities

### Safe state access

```r
#' Get a state value with a default (like ?? in JavaScript)
#' @param state The graph state list
#' @param key The state channel name
#' @param default Default value if missing
state_get <- function(state, key, default = NULL) {
  val <- state[[key]]
  if (is.null(val) || (is.character(val) && !nzchar(val))) default else val
}

# Usage in a node
my_node <- function(state) {
  count <- state_get(state, "count", 0)
  history <- state_get(state, "history", list())
  # ...
}
```

### State inspection

```r
#' Print the current state (useful for debugging)
print_state <- function(state) {
  cat("=== Current State ===\n")
  for (key in names(state)) {
    val <- state[[key]]
    if (is.data.frame(val)) {
      cat(key, ":\n"); print(head(val, 3))
    } else if (is.list(val) && length(val) > 0) {
      cat(key, ":", length(val), "items\n")
      str(head(val, 3))
    } else if (is.character(val)) {
      cat(key, ":", substr(val, 1, 100), "\n")
    } else {
      cat(key, ":", val, "\n")
    }
  }
  cat("=====================\n")
}

# Use in a node for debugging
debug_node <- function(state) {
  print_state(state)
  # ... your logic
}
```

## Reusable Graph Builders

### Linear pipeline builder

```r
#' Create a linear pipeline graph from a list of node functions
#' @param name Graph name
#' @param nodes Named list of node functions
#' @return A compiled LgGraph
linear_pipeline <- function(name, nodes) {
  node_names <- names(nodes)

  # All pipelines share the same simple state
  g <- lg_graph(name,
    state = list(
      input = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
      output = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
      step_count = list(type = "number", reducer = "overwrite")
    ))

  # Add each node
  for (nm in node_names) {
    g <- lg_add_node(g, nm, nodes[[nm]])
  }

  # Chain them together
  for (i in seq_len(length(node_names) - 1)) {
    g <- lg_add_edge(g, node_names[i], node_names[i + 1])
  }

  lg_compile(g)
}

# Usage
pipeline <- linear_pipeline("text_pipeline", list(
  extract = function(state) {
    result <- lg_call_model(list(user_msg(paste("Extract key points:", state$input))))
    list(updates = list(output = result))
  },
  expand = function(state) {
    result <- lg_call_model(list(user_msg(paste("Expand:", state$output))))
    list(updates = list(output = result))
  },
  polish = function(state) {
    result <- lg_call_model(list(user_msg(paste("Polish:", state$output))))
    list(updates = list(output = result))
  }
))

result <- pipeline$invoke("R is great for data science")
```

### Conditional router builder

```r
#' Create a routing graph from a classifier function and handler functions
#' @param name Graph name
#' @param classifier_fn Function(state) -> string (route key)
#' @param handlers Named list of handler functions
#' @return A compiled LgGraph
route_graph <- function(name, classifier_fn, handlers) {
  handler_names <- names(handlers)

  g <- lg_graph(name,
    state = list(
      input = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
      route = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
      output = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite")
    ))

  # The classifier node
  classify_fn <- function(state) {
    route <- classifier_fn(state)
    goto <- if (route %in% handler_names) route else handler_names[1]
    list(updates = list(input = state$input, route = route), goto = goto)
  }

  g <- lg_add_node(g, "classify", classify_fn)

  # Each handler
  for (nm in handler_names) {
    g <- lg_add_node(g, nm, handlers[[nm]])
  }

  lg_compile(g)
}

# Usage
graph <- route_graph("support_router",
  classifier_fn = function(state) {
    text <- tolower(state$input)
    if (grepl("billing|charge|payment|refund", text)) "billing"
    else if (grepl("error|bug|install|crash", text)) "technical"
    else "general"
  },
  handlers = list(
    billing = function(state) {
      result <- lg_call_model(list(sys_msg("You are a billing specialist."), user_msg(state$input)))
      list(updates = list(output = result))
    },
    technical = function(state) {
      result <- lg_call_model(list(sys_msg("You are a tech support agent."), user_msg(state$input)))
      list(updates = list(output = result))
    },
    general = function(state) {
      result <- lg_call_model(list(sys_msg("You are a helpful assistant."), user_msg(state$input)))
      list(updates = list(output = result))
    }
  )
)
```

### Loop builder (with max iterations)

```r
#' Create a graph that loops a node until a condition is met
#' @param name Graph name
#' @param body_fn The node function to repeat
#' @param condition_fn Function(state) -> TRUE to continue, FALSE to stop
#' @param max_iterations Safety cap
#' @return A compiled LgGraph
loop_graph <- function(name, body_fn, condition_fn, max_iterations = 10) {
  g <- lg_graph(name,
    state = list(
      input = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
      iteration = list(type = "number", reducer = "overwrite"),
      output = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite")
    ))

  loop_fn <- function(state) {
    iter <- (state$iteration %||% 0) + 1

    # Run the body
    result <- body_fn(state)

    # Check condition
    new_state <- modifyList(state, result$updates %||% list())
    new_state$iteration <- iter

    should_continue <- condition_fn(new_state) && iter < max_iterations

    if (should_continue) {
      c(result, list(updates = c(result$updates %||% list(), list(iteration = iter)),
                     goto = "loop"))
    } else {
      c(result, list(updates = c(result$updates %||% list(), list(iteration = iter))))
    }
  }

  g <- g |>
    lg_add_node("loop", loop_fn) |>
    lg_add_edge("loop", "loop") |>
    lg_compile()

  g
}

# Usage: keep refining until the answer is long enough
refiner <- loop_graph(
  "text_refiner",
  body_fn = function(state) {
    text <- state$output %||% state$input
    improved <- lg_call_model(list(
      sys_msg("Improve the text. Make it more detailed."),
      user_msg(text)
    ))
    list(updates = list(output = improved))
  },
  condition_fn = function(state) {
    nchar(state$output %||% "") < 200
  },
  max_iterations = 5
)
```

## Prompt Library

A collection of reusable system prompts for common agent types:

```r
prompts <- list(
  data_analyst = paste(
    "You are a data analyst. You help users understand their data.",
    "When given a data frame, you summarize, analyze, and visualize.",
    "Always explain your methodology and interpret results."
  ),

  code_reviewer = paste(
    "You are an R code reviewer. You check for:",
    "- Correctness and logic errors",
    "- Performance issues",
    "- Style and readability",
    "- Security vulnerabilities",
    "Provide specific, actionable feedback with code examples."
  ),

  technical_writer = paste(
    "You are a technical writer. You create clear, accurate documentation.",
    "Use active voice, define jargon, and include examples.",
    "Structure content with headings and bullet points."
  ),

  researcher = paste(
    "You are a research assistant. You find, synthesize, and present information.",
    "Distinguish between facts and inferences.",
    "Cite sources when possible."
  ),

  tutor = paste(
    "You are a patient, encouraging tutor.",
    "Explain concepts step by step.",
    "Use analogies and examples.",
    "Check understanding by asking questions."
  ),

  summarizer = paste(
    "You are a summarizer. You create concise, accurate summaries.",
    "Capture key points and main conclusions.",
    "Preserve the author's intent and tone."
  )
)

# Usage
agent <- lg_connect()
result <- agent$invoke("Explain linear regression")
# Or with a graph node:
node <- function(state) {
  result <- lg_call_model(list(
    sys_msg(prompts$tutor),
    user_msg(state$input)
  ))
  list(updates = list(output = result))
}
```

## Model Configuration Helper

```r
#' Configure langgraphr with a specific provider
#' @param provider One of "openai", "deepseek", "ollama", "custom"
#' @param api_key API key (or NULL for local models)
#' @param model Model name
#' @param base_url Custom base URL (for custom provider)
lg_config <- function(provider = c("deepseek", "openai", "ollama", "custom"),
                      api_key = NULL, model = NULL, base_url = NULL) {
  provider <- match.arg(provider)

  config <- switch(provider,
    openai = list(
      base_url = "https://api.openai.com/v1",
      model = model %||% "gpt-4o-mini",
      key = api_key %||% Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
    ),
    deepseek = list(
      base_url = "https://api.deepseek.com",
      model = model %||% "deepseek-chat",
      key = api_key %||% Sys.getenv("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY")
    ),
    ollama = list(
      base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1",
      model = model %||% "llama3.2",
      key = api_key %||% "ollama"  # ollama ignores the key
    ),
    custom = list(
      base_url = base_url,
      model = model,
      key = api_key
    )
  )

  if (nzchar(config$key)) {
    Sys.setenv(LANGGRAPHR_API_KEY = config$key)
  }
  if (!is.null(config$base_url)) {
    Sys.setenv(LANGGRAPHR_BASE_URL = config$base_url)
  }
  if (!is.null(config$model)) {
    Sys.setenv(LANGGRAPHR_MODEL = config$model)
  }

  invisible(config)
}

# Usage
lg_config("deepseek", api_key = "sk-...")
lg_config("ollama")  # local, no key needed
lg_config("openai", model = "gpt-4o")
```

## Logging and Observability

```r
#' Create a logging wrapper for node functions
#' @param fn A node function
#' @param name Node name for logging
#' @return A wrapped function that logs entry/exit
logged_node <- function(fn, name) {
  function(state) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s] ENTER at %s\n", name, format(Sys.time())))
    start <- Sys.time()

    result <- tryCatch(
      fn(state),
      error = function(e) {
        cat(sprintf("[%s] ERROR: %s\n", name, e$message))
        stop(e)
      }
    )

    elapsed <- round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start, units = "secs")), 3)
    cat(sprintf("[%s] EXIT after %ss\n", name, elapsed))

    result
  }
}

# Usage: wrap your node functions
graph <- lg_graph("debug_demo",
  state = list(value = list(type = "str"))) |>
  lg_add_node("step1", logged_node(step1_fn, "step1")) |>
  lg_add_node("step2", logged_node(step2_fn, "step2")) |>
  lg_compile()
```
